answer: Spot-audit lottery makes fake identities costly. Each identity locks a 40-credit bond to its key; each epoch a beacon draws 5% for a history check, and a pass earns a jade seal for that identity alone. A puppet cannot wander to dodge its draw, since one bond cannot cover two keys. The kth fake locks a fresh 40 credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 40,000, while an honest agent locks one and recovers it after audits. A failed check burns the bond, sends a ripple to same-source identities, and exposes rented history: a borrowed log mismatches live answers, so renter and lender both lose bonds.
